body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{CensusHandle}\), complete the secondary exhaustive characteristic-zero coordinate census for every rooted graph-query orbit \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\). For each orbit compute \(d_e(G)\) from \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\), provide a saturated rational-univariate certificate for every finite coordinate fiber, and compare the resulting degree with its prescribed-orientation coefficient, explicitly recording every strict loss caused by forced covariance relations, affine dehomogenization, or projective-infinity roots. Treat the proved five-node cubic coordinate case and the proved five-node quartic with four real positive-definite lifts as fixed base cases. The census is a regression and structural-classification problem; it is not a prerequisite for the already determined numerical frontier \(D_k(n)\) when \(n\le5\).
body.justification: This is the bounded destructive test that can invalidate the uncorrected orientation-realization conjecture before the all-size proof is attempted.
body.gap: The five-node computations of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton classify whole graphs and selected whole-fiber degrees, not every original-edge coordinate degree under the rooted excess-arrow budget in the \(S_G\)-localized prime incidence algebra.
body.consumer: The frontier proof receives certified base cases or a concrete correction term, and fasttreeid receives a complete small-instance regression suite.

obligation.what_is_open: The exhaustive characteristic-zero per-orbit coordinate census for every rooted graph-query orbit with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\), including saturated rational-univariate certificates and all strict orientation-envelope losses.
obligation.obstruction: The available exact computations certify the canonical cubic and quartic base cases but do not enumerate arbitrary bidirected supports and original-edge queries modulo rooted isomorphism, nor provide source-localized elimination certificates for every resulting orbit.
obligation.attempted: I promoted the modular quartic to a two-sided characteristic-zero Groebner certificate, proved four generic original-coordinate branches, verified all four real positive-definite lifts, and separated this completed base case from the still-missing exhaustive enumeration.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact rational certificate above proves that the specified graph in \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\) has \(d_{2\to4}(G)=4\), with four simple real queried values and four supported positive-definite lifts. Together with the canonical cubic transfer and small-size frontier results, the fixed numerical base cases are
\[
D_0(2)=1,\qquad D_k(3)=1,\qquad D_k(4)=2,
\]
for every admissible \(k\), and
\[
D_0(5)=2,\qquad D_1(5)=3,\qquad D_k(5)=4\quad(2\le k\le6).
\]
What remains is the finite per-orbit coordinate classification and its saturated certificates, not determination of these maxima.
